kind: pinned conjuncts: hand-written assertions about the LIVE registries
why: RC-02. The criterion-content oracle compares predicate-registry.json to tools/phase_content.py and fails on any difference -- which makes a HAND edit of a criterion a failing build, and makes a DERIVATION edit invisible. The recheck measured it: one hunk replacing the ('SalesAgreement','performed') spec, then `python3 tools/author_phase_content.py`, and the whole G2-01 defect is back at exit 0, 268,829 checks, with all 27 negative fixtures still rejecting. A checker that compares an artifact to a source the same author controls is not a checker. Every assertion below is written BY HAND against the live registry and is never generated from anything: author_phase_content.py does not read this file and cannot write it, so regenerating the registry from a weakened derivation now fails HERE, naming the conjunct that went missing.

how_to_read.pin: one predicate id, the findings and decisions that put each requirement there, and the `require` rows that must hold of its body in the committed predicate-registry.json
how_to_read.matching: a row matches when SOME node of the body carries that `op` and satisfies every constraint on the row. Structural containment only: a body may carry more than is pinned, never less.
how_to_read.negated: false (the default) requires a matching node that is NOT beneath a `not`; true requires one that IS. Without this, wrapping a pinned conjunct in `not` would satisfy a containment check while inverting the requirement.
how_to_read.states_exactly: the binding's `states` list must equal this set. A superset is a weakening -- `['delivered','proposed']` admits the exact counterexample AD-013 was decided to refuse -- and a subset is a different requirement than the one recorded.
how_to_read.closed_key_set: validate_contracts.py declares the constraint keys it reads and REFUSES any other key in a row. A pin whose constraint the checker silently ignored would be the same defect one layer up: a control that reads as enforcement while nothing checks it.

checked_by: validate_contracts.py: each pin against predicate-registry.json directly, with no import of tools/phase_content.py
validate_contracts.py: coverage -- every finding id swept out of registers/review-findings.json is pinned here or declared in `unpinnable` with a reason
fixtures/negative/r13-derivation-weakened-then-regenerated: patches tools/phase_content.py, regenerates with author_phase_content.py, and must be REJECTED by these pins

unpinnable.why: A coverage finding about what the specification chapters SAY, closed by prose in the residue lane. No predicate expresses it, so a conjunct pin would be a pin on something else wearing its id.
This file IS the repair for RC-02. Pinning a conjunct 'for RC-02' would be circular; what enforces it is the coverage check below plus fixtures/negative/r13-derivation-weakened-then-regenerated.

A check on the relation between a criterion's `requires` sentence and its conjuncts, which is a property of every criterion rather than of any one predicate. Implemented in validate_contracts.py as the requires/conjuncts agreement check.
A property of the negative-fixture suite, not of the registry. Implemented as fixtures/negative/MANIFEST.json and the count ratchet in tools/run_negative_fixtures.py.
A property of how the runner resolves its own root. Implemented as the symlink refusal in tools/run_negative_fixtures.py.
A prose gap: `terminated_with_residuals` appears in no specification chapter. The phase-meaning row in chapter 03 closes it; no conjunct can.

pins.why: The original (d): `performed` demanded byte-identical field_paths to `accepted`, the agreement had no relation to a Fulfillment, and the only native object reachable was the payment -- so a buyer could pay, the Fulfillment stay `proposed`, every Obligation stay `recognized`, and the sale reach `performed` with nothing objecting. AD-013 decides it: delivery, not payment. These three rows ARE that decision, and the recheck's one-hunk weakening removed all three at once.

require.why: the agreement must NAME its own Fulfillment and its obligations; without these two paths the phases below bind to nothing

AD-013: that Fulfillment is currently `delivered` and every linked Obligation is `discharged` or `transferred`. `optional: true` on either would readmit the counterexample with the field simply absent.
AD-013: the correlated native object is the DELIVERY. `result: "performed"` is what it said before the repair and correlates the sale to the charge.

pins.why: G2-02: terminating a sale asserted no closure. `terminated_with_residuals` is the state that exists to hold a non-empty due set with an accepted custodian, so a criterion that stopped requiring the duties or the custodian would make the split between the two terminal states decorative.

require.why: residuals means surviving duties AND a named owner for them
AD-014: the custodian of the residuals has ACCEPTED. A proposed assignment is a nominee, not a custodian.
the residual window is bounded in time; without it a sale sits in residuals indefinitely and the state becomes a parking lot

pins.why: G2-05: delivery must be established by an independently observed result correlated to the delivery adapter's own native object, never by the payment.

require.why: the receipts the milestones require, and the milestones themselves
a currently accepted performer delivered it
AD-013: correlation against the delivery. A settled charge is evidence about money and says nothing about whether the service arrived.

require.why: an empty reservation list is the exact shape the finding names

require.why: either burden was observed, or the account states `none_observed` with a reason, a window and a responsible assignment. Deleting the second disjunct restores the silent `[]`; deleting the first makes observation unrecordable.
the money halves the burden account sits beside

pins.why: G4-08: the schema omitted `competence_requirement_ref` from `required` while this criterion demanded it, so two implementers derive different packets from one contract -- and the stricter reading destroyed the case DIRECTIVE.md §1.6 most wants preserved, a pure taste decision with no competence prerequisite to name.

require.why: the packet states its competence footing EXACTLY ONCE, as a disjunction. Collapsing it either way is the finding: demand the ref and taste decisions cannot reach `ready`; demand neither and nothing states the footing.
the dependency graph over the children is acyclic -- a packet that is its own prerequisite is `ready` under any evidence rule

pinned_transitions_why: A conjunct pin holds a guard to what it must DEMAND. It says nothing about whether the edge exists at all, and RC-01 was exactly that shape of defect: every guard was well formed, every criterion was sourced, and a delivery that failed in flight had nowhere to go. Deleting a transition is a one-line edit to record-registry.json that no check in this package noticed -- phase reachability is not checked, and a phase with fewer ways in is not a phase with fewer conjuncts. These rows are hand-written for the same reason the conjunct pins are: nothing derives them, so regenerating cannot satisfy them.

pinned_transitions.why: A delivery that fails IN FLIGHT. Without this edge `delivering` exits only to `delivered` or `superseded`, so the only route to `failed` runs through a delivery that was correlated -- which is the contradiction RC-01 names.
Refunding an undelivered sale -- the commonest refund there is -- was unrepresentable while `refunded` had one inbound edge, from `delivered`.
The other half of the same requirement: `refunded` is reachable from BOTH, and a repair that added one route by deleting the other would satisfy a looser reading of the finding.
RC-08: without it the generic validation branch and the delivery branch are disjoint, so a validated Fulfillment can only be delivered by a route that skipped validation.
The edge AD-013's delivery evidence hangs on. Its conjuncts are pinned above; this pins that there is an edge for them to be conjuncts OF.
The route OUT of residuals. Without it `terminated_with_residuals` is a terminal state that keeps its duties forever, which is a different contract from the one AD-014 decided.

requires_waivers_why: RC-03. `requires` and `conjuncts` are independent fields of one spec and nothing compared them, so a criterion could state one requirement and demand another -- which is what the weakened derivation produced: the sentence still promised delivery over a body that had stopped asking for it. Measured before any waiver: 774 criteria examined, 0 failing the field-path rule, 17 failing the phase-name rule, every one of the 17 a phase-kind synonym for the criterion's OWN phase. Each waiver below names the exact tokens it excuses, so a new unmatched phase on a waived criterion still fails.

requires_waivers.why: The sentence names `proposed`, which is the PHASE-KIND entry this content was authored from, while AgentTemplate spells the same phase `draft`. So the token is a second name for the criterion's own phase and not a requirement about a related record -- there is nothing for a `related_phases` binding to hold. A reviewer can dispute this, and the dispute has a cure: make the kind-level prose in tools/phase_content.py say the record's own phase name. That is 17 sentences across the corpus and it was out of scope here; what is NOT in dispute is that the body demands what the sentence demands.
